tool_input.command:
gh pr create --title "fix(email): doctor falls back to identity-scoped config like status" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

`beadle-email doctor` never fell back to the per-identity `email.json` config the way `status` already did — it always loaded the legacy root `~/.punt-labs/beadle/email.json`, so `doctor` reported the wrong config for any identity-scoped setup (`[!] config FAIL` even when the real, in-effect config was fine).

What started as that one-line fix grew, across 6 rounds of local review, into a full audit and consolidation of every identity-config-resolution call site in the codebase — the same precedence rule was independently duplicated (with inconsistent, sometimes unsafe semantics) in 5+ places.

## What changed

- **One shared implementation**: `email.LoadIdentityConfig` (internal/email/config.go) is now the single place the identity-scoped-config-with-fallback precedence rule lives. Every caller — `doctor`, `status`, `list`/`search`/`read`/`send`/`reply`/`move`/`mark`/`folders`, the background poller, `set_poll_interval`, and the MCP tools' `resolveIdentityAndConfig` — now calls it instead of re-implementing the rule.
- **Fail-closed on corruption**: a corrupt/malformed identity config is now a hard error everywhere (matching the one caller — `poller.go` — that already got this right), never silently masked by a fallback to a different file. Before this, `send`/`list`/etc. could silently use a stale config if the identity config was corrupt.
- **Explicit `-c`/`--config` honored consistently**: all 10 user-facing commands that declare `-c` now treat it as an absolute override, skipping identity-config lookup entirely, via `cmd.Flags().Changed("config")`.
- **Panic risk removed**: the background poller and two MCP tool handlers no longer eagerly evaluate a panicking path-resolution helper as a call argument — a `HOME`-resolution failure now returns a clean error instead of crashing the daemon/server.
- `internal/daemon/handler.go`'s loader is unchanged (deliberately different semantics — no fallback, since it already has an established identity) but now has a comment explaining why, so a future dedup pass doesn't fold it in by mistake.

## Also included (unrelated, rollback-coherent, discovered during this session's laptop setup)

- Removed `.claude/hooks/agents-in-background.sh` and its registration — a PreToolUse hook that unconditionally blocked every `Agent` tool call by requiring a `run_in_background` parameter this Claude Code build's `Agent` tool doesn't expose, making delegation impossible in this repo.
- A doc-comment-only fix on `internal/daemon/handler.go`.

## Verification playbook

- `make check` green after every commit (23 commits total).
- Manually rebuilt and ran `beadle-email doctor`/`status`/`install` against the real, live identity setup on this laptop at each stage — confirmed the reported config path is always the one actually in effect, including the corrupt-config fail-closed path and explicit `-c` override.
- 6 rounds of independent local review (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, pr-test-analyzer) against the accumulating diff; each round's findings were fixed and re-reviewed until a round found no code defect (round 7's verdict: "no seventh code round needed... ship" — the one residual finding was a comment-accuracy issue, fixed directly).
- New test coverage: `email.LoadIdentityConfig` (all precedence branches), CLI-level tests driving `doctorCmd`/`statusCmd`/mail commands through their real entry point (`rootCmd.Execute()`), fail-closed regression tests for every migrated call site, and two `install`-specific tests proving `install` and a bare `doctor` invocation never disagree about which config is in effect.

Closes beadle-8gq. Follow-up items intentionally deferred to beadle-r32 (test hermeticity nit, an API-shape simplification) and beadle-2e6 (vendor `.punt-labs/ethos/` inline per repo-only policy, discovered as a blocker during this session's new-laptop setup, unrelated to this fix).
EOF
)" 2>&1
